# imgui_kit, for AI assistants

imgui_kit adds small, standalone helpers to Dear ImGui (C++, 1.93 or later, docking or master; MIT): layout helpers, a few widgets, em units, a touch layer for phones and tablets, and a mouse wheel that stays with the window it scrolls. Repository: https://github.com/pthom/imgui_kit

## Where the truth is

- `imgui_kit.h`: the whole API, one header, by `[SECTION]`: Em units, Layout, Widgets, Wheel session, Enums, Touch (ImGuiTouch). Each function has its doc comment there. Read it to check that a name exists and how to call it.
- `imgui_kit_demo.cpp`: a section per helper (its `IMGUI_DEMO_MARKER`), the usual way to call each one.
- Live, with its code beside it: https://pthom.github.io/imgui_explorer/?lib=imguikit (a section: `&demo=Layout%2FFill%20row`).
- `docs/dear_imgui_integration.md`: how the touch layer and the wheel session work inside, and what they read from Dear ImGui's internals.

## Build

Copy `imgui_kit*.h` and `imgui_kit*.cpp` beside Dear ImGui (leave out `imgui_kit_demo.cpp`, or define `IMGUI_KIT_DISABLE_DEMO`), or with CMake: `add_subdirectory(imgui_kit)` then link `imgui_kit` (it uses an existing `imgui` target). C++11, no STL in the core.

## Layout and widgets (namespace ImGuiKit)

- Sizes in em, which follow the font: `EmSize()`, `EmToVec2(w, h)`. Prefer them to pixels.
- Begin/End pairs: `BeginFillRow` / `FillRowTail` / `EndFillRow` (a widget fills the line, the items after the tail stay on the right), `BeginLabelColumn` / `Label` / `EndLabelColumn`, `BeginAlignedGroup` (right or centered), `BeginColumn`, `BeginGroupPanel`, `BeginFlow` (items that wrap).
- The layout helpers measure their parts on the previous frame: the first frame draws them hidden. Call them at each frame, with a stable id.
- Widgets: `HelpMarker` (an (i): a tooltip on hover, a popup on a click or a tap), `IconButton`, `SegmentedSwitch`, `FitText`, `ResizeHandle`.

## Touch screens and the wheel (namespace ImGuiTouch, and ImGuiKit::SetupWheelSession)

Set up once, after `ImGui::CreateContext()`; each then runs at each frame through Dear ImGui's context hooks (nothing to call per frame):

```cpp
ImGuiTouch::Setup();                    // swipe, long press, pinch
ImGuiKit::SetupWheelSession();          // the wheel stays with the window it scrolls
#ifdef __EMSCRIPTEN__
ImGuiTouch::SetupEmscripten();          // after the backend's init: the browser's fingers and pointer type
ImGuiTouch::SetupEmscriptenKeyboard();  // the phone's keyboard for text fields
#endif
```

The traps:
- A widget that a finger drags (a canvas, a knob): `ImGuiTouch::SetItemTakesDrags()` right after it (`ImGuiTouchAxis_Any` by default). Otherwise a drag scrolls the window, and the widget gets the finger only after a hold.
- A widget dragged along one axis (a slider): `ImGuiTouch::SetItemTakesDrags(ImGuiTouchAxis_X)` right after it: a drag along that axis moves it, a drag across scrolls the window. Dear ImGui's own sliders and drags do it with no call when the build has `IMGUI_HAS_ITEM_DRAG_AXIS_CALLBACK` (Dear ImGui Bundle's fork); with upstream Dear ImGui, call it after them.
- Two fingers on a widget (otherwise they scale the font), one call right after it: `ImGuiTouch::ItemPinch()` returns the gesture (`ImGuiTouchPinch`: `Center`, `CenterDelta`, `ScaleDelta`, `Scale`, `Started`, `Ended`, `Kind`) for a widget that zooms and pans itself; for an existing widget that zooms with the wheel, `ImGuiTouch::SetItemPinchAsWheel(wheel_zoom_factor, delivery)` (1.1 = +10% per wheel unit; `ImGuiTouchPinchDelivery_WheelNotches` if it reads only the wheel's sign) and `ImGuiTouch::SetItemTwoFingerPanAsMouseDrag(button)`. `RectPinch()`, `SetRectPinchAsWheel()`, `SetRectTwoFingerPanAsMouseDrag()` for a rectangle (a plot). An item that calls `ItemPinch()` needs an id (an `InvisibleButton`).
- A widget that reads the wheel claims it while hovered: `if (ImGui::SetItemKeyOwner(ImGuiKey_MouseWheelY)) ...`. Otherwise the wheel session gives the wheel to the window that scrolls.
- In a browser, the canvas must have the id "canvas".
- Which backends report fingers, the touch source and the keyboard, and what to add for the others: the README, "What each backend reports". In short: a browser (with the kit's Emscripten setup) is complete; SDL, Win32 and Android report the touch source but no fingers (no pinch); GLFW on Linux and macOS cannot tell a finger.
- A native app (iOS, Android) reports each finger with `ImGuiTouch::AddFingerEvent(id, pos, phase)` (for the pinch; `ImGuiTouchPhase_Cancelled` when the system takes the touch over), and its keyboard with `ImGuiTouch::SetKeyboardInsets()`: see `examples/ios_touch_demo/main.mm`.
- An app that sleeps when idle keeps drawing while `ImGuiTouch::IsAnimating()` is true.
- To try it on a desktop: `ImGuiTouch::GetConfig().SimulateTouch = true` (the mouse plays a finger).
- With Dear ImGui's Test Engine: set the kit up before `ImGuiTestEngine_Start()` (hooks run in the order they were added).
- Hello ImGui sets all of this up itself: its settings are `RunnerParams::touchConfig` and `RunnerParams::wheelSession`.

## Python

Dear ImGui Bundle binds the kit as `imgui_bundle.imgui_kit` (snake_case names; each Begin/End pair is also a context manager, e.g. `with imgui_kit.fill_row("id") as row:`). Its guide for AI assistants: https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/llms.txt, and the kit's API in plain text: https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/llms/api/imgui_kit.txt
